title: Similarity of climate and geology is described as ruling out environmental causes
evidence: The passage says the islands were similar in climate and geology and otters appeared to be the deciding factor. Choice C and the overall explanation say this rules out environmental differences/other causes.
proposedFix: Retain C. Say that similarity in climate and geology strengthens the inference that otters explain the difference; do not say an observational comparison rules out all environmental causes.
acceptanceTests: ["C remains the strongest quoted support.", "No explanation claims similarity proves causation or excludes every possible environmental difference."]

title: Countless failures do not logically disprove a majority-survival claim
evidence: Choice A says most Roman concrete structures still stand. Its explanation calls this contradicted by Countless others have long since collapsed. Countless gives no proportion.
proposedFix: Keep A incorrect and D correct, but call A unsupported: the passage supplies no total or fraction showing most survive. Explain that the survivors may be an unusually well-built subset.
acceptanceTests: ["Explanation distinguishes unsupported from contradicted.", "No unstated numerical majority is inferred from countless."]

title: Not disproving a study is treated as proving its effect real
evidence: Paragraph 5 says the later finding did not mean the original study was wrong. Q135 D says They showed a real effect; both explanations equate not wrong with real. Q136 commonTrap says an average near zero points toward the original study being wrong.
proposedFix: Revise Q135 D to: Their result cannot be assumed to occur in every setting. Keep Q136 C as the supporting sentence. Explain that the later evidence limits generalization and does not by itself establish that the original result was false or prove it universally reliable. Revise both items and traps together.
acceptanceTests: ["The supported inference concerns generalization across settings.", "No statement converts failure to disprove into proof.", "No statement treats a near-zero pooled average alone as proof the original study was false."]

title: Part B lacks the Part A question in its own record
evidence: Q135 introduces a two-part question and contains Part A; Q136 asks for support for the answer to Part A without restating Part A. Both are independent MC4 records sharing only a passageId in the supplied content.
proposedFix: Make Q136 self-contained by restating the supported claim, or create explicit linked-part metadata and enforce atomic selection plus A-before-B ordering in every delivery path. Until one approach is verified, do not serve Q136 independently. Delivery verification is a separate source-code check, not established by this content audit.
acceptanceTests: ["Selecting Q136 alone still yields an answerable prompt, or selection automatically includes Q135 first.", "Question limits, randomization, review, saved sessions and adaptive paths cannot orphan or reverse the pair.", "The pair remains two explicitly scored responses if intended."]

title: Trap teaches a sweeping claim about SHSAT similes
evidence: commonTrap says On the SHSAT, a simile like this almost always describes a feeling or mood. That empirical test rule is not established and encourages a shortcut.
proposedFix: Replace the blanket test claim with a passage-specific explanation: the hidden notebook and Lena’s hesitation make this simile convey suspense about disclosure.
acceptanceTests: ["Trap explains this passage’s language without an unverified always/almost-always SHSAT rule."]

title: Explanation reverses or invents the direction of the plant move
evidence: Paragraph 11 says Lena moved plants to the other side of the classroom because of the radiator and wonders whether the first group was warmer. Choice C and both solutionExplanation copies instead say she moved the plants near a radiator.
proposedFix: Change all occurrences to: Lena realizes she changed the plants’ windowsill between trials, so heat rather than music may explain the different results. Do not assert that the March plants moved closer to the radiator.
acceptanceTests: ["Choice C explanation, top-level solutionExplanation and ms.solutionExplanation agree.", "No explanation says the second-trial plants moved near the radiator.", "Keys remain C and E."]

title: Sentence stem includes a two-sentence keyed quotation
evidence: Q147 D contains His jaw was tight. For the first time all morning, he wasn’t whistling. Q159 C contains You are nervous, though you don’t say so. So I gave you a bright morning and a woman who said welcome. Both stems ask Which sentence.
proposedFix: Change Which sentence from the passage to Which quotation from the passage in both stems. Preserve the full two-sentence evidence and keys.
acceptanceTests: ["Stem accurately describes each answer unit.", "Q147 remains D and Q159 remains C."]

title: Table is described as making a decline directly comparable despite mismatched measures
evidence: Key C says the table makes the decline and recovery easier to compare; its explanation says readers can see the fall and rise at a glance. The early 1947 row counts turtles on one beach in one day; 1985 counts worldwide annual nests. Q6 B correctly warns that such units are not directly comparable. Comparable pairs in the table show increases (1985→2009 worldwide nests; 1996→2012 Texas nests), not a like-for-like decline.
proposedFix: Revise C to: It gathers counts reported in the article and identifies where, when, and what was counted. Explain the two valid like-for-like increase comparisons and say the historical decline/recent reversal are described in prose rather than directly measured by comparable declining rows in this table.
acceptanceTests: ["Q6 and Q7 use the same rule for comparable data.", "No direct numeric fall is inferred between 1947 turtles and 1985 nests.", "C remains uniquely correct."]

title: Distractor rationale treats temperature and moisture sensitivity as exclusive
evidence: Choice B explanation says Warmth affects temperature-sensitive trees, not the moisture-sensitive tree described here. The passage describes dominant growth constraints, not immunity to all other environmental influences.
proposedFix: Replace with: The stated evidence concerns moisture-dependent growth, so it supports dry years rather than establishing unusually warm years. In the passage’s temperature example, warmth is associated with wider, not narrower, rings.
acceptanceTests: ["Key stays C.", "Explanation rejects the unsupported temperature inference without claiming warmth cannot affect a moisture-sensitive tree."]

title: Rationale denies a behavioral change mentioned elsewhere
evidence: Choice C explanation says she never says she changed how she behaved, but paragraph 3 says I strove to conduct myself as befitted a Fellow Citizen.
proposedFix: Explain that the passage does not rank honesty above every other virtue or specifically say she stopped trying to escape punishment. Acknowledge her more general sense of civic responsibility.
acceptanceTests: ["The rationale does not deny paragraph 3’s stated effort to change conduct.", "Key B is unchanged."]

title: Explanation analyzes italics absent from supplied passage text
evidence: Choice C and solutionExplanation say the italics on feel stress emotion; the supplied passage body has plain feel, although answer-choice strings contain asterisk markup.
proposedFix: Either restore verified original emphasis in the passage through supported rendering, or remove the assertion about italics and base the explanation on the explicit understood/feel contrast. The latter is the smallest content-only fix.
acceptanceTests: ["Explanation references only typography actually visible to students.", "If restoring emphasis, validate passage and choice rendering in all clients.", "Key C remains supported without relying on formatting."]

title: An appearance claim is rejected as though it claimed literal rotation
evidence: Choice B says the city looks as if it is spinning. Its explanation rejects it because the speaker, not the city, is spinning. The speaker’s motion could produce that apparent motion; the decisive issue is that B does not explain guess.
proposedFix: Keep D best, but explain that B may account for whirling alone and misses the city shrinking into an uncertain guess. Optionally strengthen the stem to ask what the city’s progression from dew-drop to guess conveys about the speaker’s view.
acceptanceTests: ["Do not equate looks as if with literally is.", "D is justified using tiny→dew-drop→guess and increasing height.", "Reviewer checks B cannot be equally complete for the final stem."]

title: Shaken with laughter is treated as direct evidence of fear
evidence: Key B is correct, but its explanation says Shaken shows fear. In Shaken with a giddy laughter, shaken describes the laughter; afraid is the direct fear evidence.
proposedFix: State that giddy laughter and blissfully convey delight while afraid conveys fear. Use the full phrase blissfully afraid to show simultaneous emotions.
acceptanceTests: ["Key B remains unchanged.", "Choice and overall explanations cite afraid for fear rather than misreading shaken with laughter."]

title: Passage overstates the amount of extra bridge wire
evidence: Paragraph 6 and Q7 C say thousands of additional wires were added because of deficient wire. The National Register nomination reports 152 extra wires per cable (5,434 rather than 5,282), hundreds across four cables rather than thousands.
proposedFix: Replace thousands of additional wires with additional high-quality wire in the passage and its exact quotation in Q7 C. This preserves the inference without introducing a disputable precision claim.
acceptanceTests: ["Passage paragraph 6 and Q7 C remain exact matches.", "All nine bridge questions are reread against the edited passage.", "No copy continues to say thousands of extra wires."]
externalSource: https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/763eefb2-3e0e-44e3-be5e-c7bdd9608e7b/ (National Register nomination, PDF p.6, continuation p.5)

title: No-new-cases wording overlooks the 1978 laboratory-associated cases
evidence: Paragraph 7 moves from the last naturally occurring 1977 case to two more years of searching that turned up no new cases. WHO records laboratory-associated cases in Birmingham in 1978.
proposedFix: Qualify the sentence to say continued surveillance found no further naturally occurring cases, then retain the 1979 commission/1980 WHO declaration sequence. Optional brief parenthesis may distinguish the 1978 laboratory incident.
acceptanceTests: ["No unqualified assertion of zero smallpox cases after 1977.", "ELA-RC-119 through 124 remain supported, especially chronology."]

title: Jam display conditions are incorrectly assigned to different days
evidence: Paragraph 2 says 24 varieties were displayed on some days and six on other days. Iyengar’s own account says the booth switched between the assortments within hours.
proposedFix: Replace those two clauses with: The researchers alternated between a display of twenty-four varieties of jam and a display of six. Retain the correctly identified stopping and purchasing percentages.
acceptanceTests: ["Passage does not claim conditions were separated by day.", "The 60/40 stopping rates and 30/3 purchase rates retain their correct denominators.", "ELA-RC-131 through 136 are rechecked after editing."]
externalSource: https://business.columbia.edu/sites/default/files-efs/pubfiles/5228/better%20choosing%20experience.pdf (Iyengar and Agrawal, PDF p.4, original magazine p.3)

title: Saw changes location within opening description
evidence: Paragraph 2 places the table saw in the middle of the room; paragraph 3 says it sat in the corner. No move is described.
proposedFix: Use a consistent location, e.g. revise paragraph 3 to while the saw stood nearby like a dog I was forbidden to pet, and update the exact quotation in ELA-RC-164 plus any references to corner.
acceptanceTests: ["Passage and Q164 quotation match exactly.", "No conflicting center/corner locations remain.", "The off-limits temptation comparison remains intact."]

title: Nine direct definition items differ from observed current official item style
evidence: All nine have a uniquely supported definition in their supplied passages. The separate official-scope review searched all 200 ELA items in current practice forms A–D and found word/phrase effect, contribution, contextual paraphrase and inference tasks, but no dictionary/synonym-choice stems. This observation is not a DOE prohibition.
proposedFix: For strict exam-style fidelity, rewrite these nine as passage-dependent effect/function/inference items, retaining the passage and stable item ID only if versioning policy permits. Do not delete all RC-VOC items: ten other tagged items already test contextual/figurative interpretation.
acceptanceTests: ["Each replacement requires the passage rather than only vocabulary knowledge.", "Four plausible alternatives, exactly one best answer, evidence-based rationale and trap.", "Replacement does not duplicate another question in its passage set.", "Record old/new version and obtain editorial approval."]
externalSource: Official-scope worker report; current DOE/Pearson A–D practice forms. Full official-source ledger is supplied separately by the scope audit.
